conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Lopez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to help you feel supported in these early weeks of motherhood. To get a quick picture of how you’ve been feeling, I’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s a short 10-question tool that screens for mood and anxiety symptoms that sometimes show up after birth, and it includes a question about thoughts of self-harm. Everything you share stays between us unless you or your baby are in danger. We’ll take it one question at a time, focusing only on the past seven days. Ready to begin?

Question 1: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the lighter side of things, or has that felt difficult for you?

[Voice a little quiet, eyes shifting between the baby in the carrier and Dr. Lopez]

Lately it’s been… pretty hard. I still laugh sometimes—like yesterday my husband sent a silly meme and I chuckled—but it fades fast. Most of the day I just feel this heaviness, so even when something’s funny, it’s like I can’t really feel it, you know.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Mostly I’ve had to force it, if I’m honest. I’ll smile when someone cracks a joke, but it doesn’t feel natural—kind of like I’m watching myself from outside. I guess I’d say “not so much now” rather than “yes, as much as I always could.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—meeting a friend for coffee, even just a walk—but this week nothing feels worth the effort. I still do a couple of things because I think I “should,” but the spark isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens a lot. If the baby spits up more than usual or won’t settle, my head jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I know, logically, babies just fuss, but I still catch myself thinking it’s my fault—like I’m already failing him somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll just be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my chest gets tight—worrying the latch’s wrong, or he’ll choke, or I’ll fall asleep and drop him. Nothing’s actually happening, but the thoughts keep spinning. I can calm myself after a few minutes, but it keeps popping up.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Yes… a couple of times. Once, I was folding laundry and my heart started racing out of nowhere, like I was in danger, but nothing was wrong. It only lasted a few minutes, but it was scary.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days it feels like I’m barely treading water. I’ll be trying to answer one text, the baby starts crying, the dog barks, and suddenly I’m on the verge of tears because it all piles up at once. I manage, but it takes every ounce of energy.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah, that’s been happening. I lie down exhausted, but my brain won’t shut off—replaying every little thing I did with the baby, worrying I missed something. A couple nights I couldn’t fall asleep for a couple hours, and when I do drift off I wake up again with these anxious thoughts racing.
I have felt sad or miserable
Most of the time. It’s like there’s this gray cloud that follows me around. I’ll have a few okay minutes here and there, but the overall feeling is just… down and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Once was when he wouldn’t nap no matter what I tried, and I just sat in the rocker with him on my shoulder and cried—quiet sobs so I wouldn’t scare him. Another night I was heating up dinner and the tears started rolling for no clear reason.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[Voice drops, eyes on the floor]  
Once or twice in the past week, yeah… just fleeting. Like I’ll be holding the bottle and suddenly picture smashing it against my arm or thinking maybe I shouldn’t wake up tomorrow. I don’t want to do it, and I haven’t made any plan—I love this baby—I just… the thought pops in and scares me.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed:
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia (Q2, Q8, Q9)
- Loss of pleasure/enjoyment; activities completed only out of obligation (Q1, Q2)
- Excessive self-blame and guilt regarding infant care (Q3)
- Marked anxiety (near-daily), intrusive worries, and two recent unexpected panic episodes (Q4, Q5)
- Feeling overwhelmed and unable to cope with routine demands (Q6)
- Sleep-onset and maintenance difficulties linked to rumination (Q7)

Pattern: Symptoms present "most days" for at least the past week, causing distress and functional difficulty.

Safety flag: Fleeting, unwanted thoughts of self-harm ("picture smashing bottle against arm," "maybe I shouldn’t wake up tomorrow") without intent or plan (Q10).

Screening significance: High endorsement consistent with probable major depressive episode with anxious features; self-harm ideation warrants immediate safety assessment and expedited referral for psychiatric evaluation and support.
